data.description:
## Context

Bug 8185 proved that physically deleting committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, DONE_ENRICH, and TICKET_DIGEST UUID events makes independently valid stale-clone histories conflict. The immediate repair restores append-only union merges by stopping those deletes. The tradeoff is unbounded per-ticket event accumulation and O(history) queue/digest scans.

## Plan

- Measure queue and digest read/gate cost against realistic repeated-enrichment histories.
- Design retention that preserves cross-clone union convergence and recovery invariants, using merge-safe compaction or an equivalent append-only representation rather than physical deletion.
- Prove the design with real two-clone stale-history tests and performance coverage before changing production behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A benchmark or deterministic performance test quantifies current per-ticket scan growth.
- [ ] The chosen retention design preserves every independently committed event or its lossless compacted representation across stale-clone merges.
- [ ] Real two-clone coverage proves clean reconvergence when retention runs independently in both clones.
- [ ] Queue and latest-digest reads have a documented and tested bound.
- [ ] The design introduces no physical delete/rename conflict for committed UUID events.
data.title: Design merge-safe retention for enrichment queue and digest history
